The pathway begins with Octadeca-6,9,12-trienoic acid, which is directly linked to 5-hydroxytryptamine receptor 1. This receptor is then identified as a target of Ginseng, and Ginseng is shown to target Protein-arginine deiminase type-3. This implies that Octadeca-6,9,12-trienoic acid may act through Ginseng to influence the activity of Protein-arginine deiminase type-3. The mechanism is likely indirect, with Octadeca-6,9,12-trienoic acid serving as a modulator that interacts with Ginseng to affect the target enzyme. The evidence supports a potential role for Octadeca-6,9,12-trienoic acid in modulating the activity of Protein-arginine deiminase type-3 via a pathway involving Ginseng.
